content.heading: Limits and costs
content.text: Courts shall not entertain as PIL a petition that is in substance a private dispute, service matter, contractual rivalry, or politically or publicity-motivated grievance. Liberalised standing is subject to the bona fide public-interest requirement. Where a petition abuses the process of the Court under the label of PIL, the Court may dismiss it at the threshold and may impose costs, including exemplary or heavy costs, on the petitioner. Costs and consequences of abuse belong to this limit; they do not alter the availability of genuine public-interest standing under Articles 32 and 226.
